examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For a reduction A≤B, construct a solver for A assuming a solver for B; undecidability then transfers from A to B, not in the reverse direction. Rice's theorem applies to nontrivial semantic properties of recognized languages, not arbitrary syntactic machine properties. CFG emptiness is decidable even though general CFG equivalence is not.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Among DFA emptiness, CFG emptiness and equivalence of two arbitrary CFGs, how many problems are decidable?

**Answer: 2.** DFA emptiness is reachability of a final state. CFG emptiness is productivity of its start variable. Arbitrary CFG equivalence is undecidable. Hence two listed problems are decidable.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A reduction must be effective and preserve both yes and no instances. Testing finitely many sample inputs cannot decide arbitrary language equivalence.

Reducing an undecidable target to a known undecidable problem does not prove the target undecidable; the direction matters.
